title: Creative catalogue: twenty-five visual axes
status_note: The following banks were materialized from the 10 October 2026 catalogue and are preserved here as usable text. They remain proposals. The catalogue's earlier statement that a second film was in progress and that zero twelve-style slots were qualified is a historical assembly snapshot; it is not today's completed-film ledger. This guide does not retroactively mark individual catalogue recipes rendered because a similarly named film exists.

records.definition: Looks straight down without perspective convergence.
records.use: Routes, layouts, traffic toys, mazes and procedural systems.
records.check: Do not infer object height from a top view; label scale if meaningful.

records.definition: Action is staged along a clear horizontal or vertical plane.
records.use: Character movement, levers, elevators and sequence lessons.
records.check: Keep contacts visible and avoid accidental depth cues.

records.definition: A parallel-projection view exposes several axes at once.
records.use: Workshops, city systems and compact multi-station stories.
records.check: Use consistent projection and disclose decorative scale choices.

records.definition: A camera sees the scene from a character-like vantage point.
records.use: Embodied travel, obstacles, effort and cinematic story scenes.
records.check: Maintain lens, horizon and spatial continuity.

records.definition: Two or more cameras show the same state and moment.
records.use: Geometry checks, assembly, ambiguous silhouettes and mechanism teaching.
records.check: Synchronize time, object identity and scale references.

records.definition: Paths, shapes and articulated planar characters.
records.use: Crisp causal diagrams and expressive economical stories.
records.check: A pan or shadow does not turn it into volumetric 3D.

records.definition: Cutouts occupy declared depth planes and move with parallax.
records.use: Rich illustrated worlds, motion comics and quiet emotional scenes.
records.check: Inspect masks and disoccluded gaps; depth is approximate.

records.definition: True volumes use deliberately visible polygonal faces.
records.use: Toy terrain, expeditions and readable block-world action.
records.check: Check real geometry and alternate angles; faceting is not a color filter.

records.definition: Modeled surfaces, real cameras, lights and object depth.
records.use: Tactile characters, turntables and spatial mechanism stories.
records.check: Check normals, contact, silhouette and native reopening.

records.definition: A true volume is cut or separated to expose its relationships.
records.use: Product anatomy, architecture and machinery explanations.
records.check: The section plane and part relationships must be geometrically valid.

records.definition: Fibers, layered edges and soft cut-paper shadows.
records.use: Editorial stories, maps and tactile explanation.
records.check: Use original/procedural or individually cleared textures.

records.definition: Soft fibers, stitched seams and diffuse light.
records.use: Warm characters, care stories and miniature objects.
records.check: Texture alone is not cloth simulation; verify deformations if claimed.

records.definition: Soft sculpted forms, roughness and designed deformation.
records.use: Character comedy, fables and tactile transformation.
records.check: Label rendered clay-style work accurately; inspect volume preservation.

records.definition: Grainy strokes and drawn construction marks.
records.use: Stepwise reasoning and field-note explanations.
records.check: Keep geometry, text and contrast legible despite texture.

records.definition: Distinct grain, glaze or specular response.
records.use: Object fables and crafted mechanisms.
records.check: Match lighting to material; do not claim physical authenticity.

records.definition: An individually cleared image contributes surface or setting detail.
records.use: Rich environments and documentary illustration.
records.check: Review each source's rights, provenance and spatial limits.

records.definition: Restrained detail, explicit labels and clear relationships.
records.use: Math, computing, mechanisms and demonstrations.
records.check: A technical look does not establish factual accuracy.

records.definition: Small original worlds, grounded characters and intentional light.
records.use: Cooperation, everyday microdrama and gentle adventure.
records.check: Preserve a complete story rather than only attractive scenery.

records.definition: Bold shapes, hatching, print texture and deliberate framing.
records.use: Editorial learning and compact visual storytelling.
records.check: Do not use texture or busy outlines to hide weak action.

records.definition: Lighting, depth and camera timing support mood.
records.use: Character scenes and journeys.
records.check: Readable action and honest source evidence remain required.

records.definition: One main action with a small supporting diagram or label.
records.use: Focused explanation and character-led teaching.
records.check: Keep the evidence readable and do not let the host cover it.

records.definition: Two states or views share one timeline.
records.use: Controlled contrasts and multiple interpretations.
records.check: State what changes and what is held fixed.

records.definition: A grid displays distinct views or moments.
records.use: Character sheets, object inspection and perspective puzzles.
records.check: Limit panels to phone-readable content; label moments versus viewpoints.

records.definition: The main object remains visible beside an internal view.
records.use: Mechanisms and hidden relationships.
records.check: Keep the inset tied to the same exact object and state.

records.definition: Actual source contributions separate into inspectable passes.
records.use: Production teaching and reusable component review.
records.check: Count only active meaningful contributions; do not double-count nested groups.
